exchanges.title: Cross-harbor token re-issuance under epoch-rewind

queries.name: re-issuance-with-epoch-rewind
queries.result: FALSE — attacker CAN derive when verifier checks current root

exchanges.observable: A token T revoked at epoch e is accepted at epoch e+1 if the verifier reads the current federation root instead of the historical root for the token's epoch.
exchanges.impact: Re-issuance attack: any revoked token is re-presentable at a peer harbor for one epoch following revocation. Bonded settlement clears against a revoked capability.

fix_construction.defense: Epoch-binding in the token preimage; verifier checks the historical federation root, not the current one. The paper now states this explicitly in §fh-3 with `MECHANIZATION:whitepaper/formal/proverif/federated-harbor/tokens/cross-harbor-issuance.pv`.

hedge.narrows: Verifiers retain a sparse log of historical roots; storage O(log epoch + recent-window). See [PLACEHOLDER-FEDLOG-§] for the storage bound (pinned to §fh-A.3 this round).

refuses_prices.prices: retention of historical root log (operators charging more for deeper history)

exchanges.title: Two-hop silent transitivity in pact composition

queries.name: two-hop-composition
queries.expected: consented(A,C) must precede accepted(C-token at A)
queries.result: FALSE — silent transitivity: paper's verify rule accepted without consent event

exchanges.observable: A presents pact registry showing A→B; B→C exists; A's verifier accepts a C-issued token without an explicit consented(A,C) event ever having been emitted.
exchanges.impact: Silent trust transitivity. Operator of A loses control over which downstream harbors their tokens flow to.

fix_construction.defense: Federation pacts are non-transitive by default. Verifier rule binds the verifying harbor's own pact-set, not the chain. Two-hop pact composition does NOT imply consented(A,C) absent an explicit attestation event.

exchanges.title: Bounded partition exceeds stated D

smell_construction.counterexample: Partition harbor H from federation for D+1 epochs. Adversary presents token T (revoked at federation level at epoch e) at H during the partition window. H accepts because pessimistic-verifier rule was not yet stated in §fh-7.

exchanges.observable: A revoked token T verifies at harbor H during a partition of length D+1, where the paper claims the bound is D.
exchanges.impact: Partition-then-spend attack. Adversary times a transaction inside the partition window.

fix_construction.defense: Two-pronged: (a) bounded propagation invariant — harbors commit in pact to max propagation delay D, bond slashes on failure; (b) pessimistic verifier — partitioned harbor refuses cross-harbor tokens until re-sync.

refuses_prices.prices: revocation propagation latency (harbors paid for faster re-sync; harbors that exceed D slash)
